summary: A Knightscope K5 security robot patrolling a California shopping mall knocked down a 16-month-old child and reportedly ran over his foot, causing minor injuries. The company disputed the family's account, and the mall docked its robots.
technical_summary: An autonomous wheeled patrol robot with sensors and cameras collided with a toddler walking ahead of his parents. The parents say it kept moving; the company says it veered and the child ran into it. The robot's obstacle detection and stopping behavior around small children failed or was disputed.

sector.quote: a robot security guard at the Stanford Shopping Center in Silicon Valley knocked down a toddler while on duty

technology.quote: The robot trundles about on wheels and uses an array of sensors and cameras to monitor its environment.

failure_mode.quote: knocked their 16-month-old to the ground and ran over one of his feet

harm_type.quote: knocked their 16-month-old to the ground and ran over one of his feet

affected_population.quote: knocked their 16-month-old to the ground and ran over one of his feet

severity.quote: X-rays taken after the incident were negative.

notes: Company and family gave conflicting accounts of how the collision occurred.

summary: A researcher's experiment suggested TikTok's account recommendations suggested people who looked physically similar to the account followed, including by race, age and disability. TikTok said recommendations rely on user behavior, not appearance or race.
technical_summary: TikTok's suggested-accounts feature uses collaborative filtering based on follow behavior. Informal tests found recommended profiles resembled the followed account in apparent race, hair, age and visible disability, which could reinforce coverage bias through a feedback loop, even without using race or photos as inputs.

technology.quote: the profiles recommended by TikTok seemed eerily, physically similar to the profile picture of the first account

failure_mode.quote: the profiles recommended by TikTok seemed eerily, physically similar to the profile picture of the first account

affected_population.quote: Following black men led to recommendations to follow more black men.
TikTok adapts 'recommendability' on hair style, body profile, age, how (un)dressed the person is, and even whether they have visible disabilities.

notes: Based on an informal experiment; at least one person could not replicate the results.

summary: A YouTuber trained a language model on a toxic 4chan board, deployed it as bots that posted thousands of messages there, and published the model online, drawing criticism from AI researchers who called it unethical.
technical_summary: An open language model was fine-tuned on millions of posts from a board known for racist, misogynistic and antisemitic content, then run as multiple bots posting about 15,000 times in 24 hours. The model was shared publicly on Hugging Face before access was restricted.

technology.quote: trained an AI using 3.3 million threads from 4chan’s infamously toxic Politically Incorrect /pol/ board

failure_mode.quote: the AI was just as vile as the posts it was trained on, spouting racial slurs and engaging with antisemitic threads
he performed human experiments without informing users, without consent or oversight

notes: Creator calls it a prank with little harm; researchers dispute this and cite lack of consent or oversight.

summary: Google Photos' automated assistant stitched three ski trip photos into a panorama that made one friend appear as a giant floating head behind trees. The odd result went viral as a harmless glitch.
technical_summary: A photo assistant automatically grouped similar frames and blended them into a panorama. Its compositing algorithm combined subjects from different shots in a way that distorted the scene, producing a surreal image. No harm resulted beyond a confusing, humorous output.

failure_mode.quote: it might turn your friend into a giant head lurking in a forest

notes: Trivial incident widely shared for humor.

summary: In Taiwan, a Tesla on Autopilot crashed into a road repair truck while its driver was not watching the road. A road worker who then placed warning signs was struck and killed by a BMW.
technical_summary: Tesla Autopilot did not detect a brightly marked repair truck, and the driver admitted he had stopped paying attention. The resulting accident scene led to a second collision with a BMW whose driver also failed to notice the warning signs, killing the worker.

failure_mode.quote: the vehicle failed to detect the road repair truck against which it crashed
Tesla driver admits he was not paying attention while autopilot was engaged.

harm_type.quote: collided with a maintenance vehicle on a highway in Taoyuan moments before a worker responding to the accident was fatally struck by a BMW

affected_population.quote: collided with a maintenance vehicle on a highway in Taoyuan moments before a worker responding to the accident was fatally struck by a BMW

severity.quote: collided with a maintenance vehicle on a highway in Taoyuan moments before a worker responding to the accident was fatally struck by a BMW

notes: The fatality resulted directly from a second, distracted driver; Autopilot's role is indirect.

summary: An app that uses AI to estimate the speed of passing cars so people can report speeding drew angry reactions from UK drivers, who called it surveillance, and its developers went anonymous after abuse.
technical_summary: Speedcam Anywhere uses computer vision to estimate vehicle speed from smartphone video, automating forensic analysis that police can use for prosecutions. Critics argue it enables citizen surveillance and abuse. App stores delayed or refused distribution.

technology.quote: a new app that uses AI to estimate the speed of a passing car

notes: Concern is potential surveillance and abuse; no concrete harm from the app is documented.

summary: An Amazon seller, suspected of using a bot, listed tens of thousands of phone cases with bizarre stock photos, including medical images and drug references, baffling and offending some shoppers.
technical_summary: An apparently automated process pulled stock photos from an unclear source and auto-generated product pages and prices for phone cases, with no sensible curation. Listings drifted toward medical and unsuitable images, and the marketplace did not screen them.

failure_mode.quote: The out-of-control algorithm currently lists over 31,000 products on Amazon, the quality of which varies wildly

affected_population.quote: The Amazon bot has generated thousands of phone cases, much to the bewilderment of shoppers

notes: Reports speculate it may be human-run rather than a bot; mechanism is unconfirmed.

summary: Researchers built a facial recognition dataset from YouTube transition videos of transgender people without their consent. It was reportedly shared with other academics and remained online for years, without ethics review.
technical_summary: A university team scraped time-lapse hormone therapy videos to train and test face recognition across gender transition. The dataset contained the videos themselves, was copied to other researchers and stayed on a public link, with no institutional ethics approval or consent from the people filmed.
developers: University of North Carolina Wilmington researchers
deployers: University of North Carolina Wilmington researchers

failure_mode.quote: 10,000 images of 38 trans people, scraped from their YouTube videos documenting their hormone therapies
the HRT Transgender Dataset still available as a Dropbox URL until April 2021
The dataset was shared with academics who subsequently shared it with their own doctoral students and researchers, again without oversight.

lifecycle_stage.quote: 10,000 images of 38 trans people, scraped from their YouTube videos documenting their hormone therapies

affected_population.quote: 10,000 images of 38 trans people, scraped from their YouTube videos documenting their hormone therapies

notes: Researcher said consent was sought but not obtained from all and that only links were shared; later research disputed this.

summary: Stanford researchers found more than 1,000 LinkedIn profiles using AI-generated faces, many used by sales outreach firms to message prospective customers. LinkedIn removed profiles that broke its rules against fake accounts.
technical_summary: Fake professional profiles with GAN-generated headshots were used to send automated-looking sales pitches, with replies routed to real salespeople. The synthetic faces evaded simple checks, letting companies bypass messaging limits and misrepresent who was contacting recipients.

sector.quote: NPR found that many of the LinkedIn profiles seem to have a far more mundane purpose: drumming up sales for companies big and small.

technology.quote: uncovered more than 1,000 LinkedIn profiles using what appear to be faces created by artificial intelligence

failure_mode.quote: uncovered more than 1,000 LinkedIn profiles using what appear to be faces created by artificial intelligence

affected_population.quote: Anyone who takes the bait gets connected to a real salesperson who tries to close the deal.

notes: Mostly commercial deception rather than disinformation; some firms said they did not authorize AI faces.

summary: A study found Google AdSense showed ads suggesting an arrest record more often when searching for names associated with Black people than for names associated with white people.
technical_summary: Ad delivery on Google search and a partner site paired racially associated first names with ads implying arrest records at very different rates, independent of actual records. The cause was unclear, possibly ad-copy selection, click feedback or caching, but the delivery showed adverse impact by race.

sector.quote: This writing investigates the delivery of these kinds of ads by Google AdSense

failure_mode.quote: statistically significant discrimination in ad delivery based on searches of 2184 racially associated personal names across two websites

affected_population.quote: On the more ad trafficked website, a black-identifying name was 25% more likely to get an ad suggestive of an arrest record.

notes: Evidence supports racial disparity; the AIID description also mentions sexism, which excerpts do not show.

summary: A French welfare office's automated system wrongly told a benefits recipient she owed 542 euros after misreading her income status, with repayment deducted automatically. A human caseworker cancelled the debt once she explained the error.
technical_summary: Welfare software assessed a case using fixed parameters and, after the claimant registered as a freelancer, ignored her salaried income and recalculated benefits, issuing a debt notice and automatic deductions. The system flagged first and left verification to humans after the claimant objected.

failure_mode.quote: The machine threatens first, humans verify later.

harm_type.quote: the welfare office tells me that I owe them 542 euros and that the amount will be automatically taken from my next payments

notes: Single first-person account; debt was cancelled within days, but the title suggests a wider pattern.

summary: After Microsoft replaced human editors at MSN with automated systems, the site illustrated a story about one member of a pop group with a photo of another mixed-race member, prompting complaints and an apology.
technical_summary: MSN's automated editorial system paired a story headline with the wrong image. Microsoft said it was not algorithmic bias but a test feature that chose an alternate photo from the article page and mismatched it to the headline, and that human editors would normally have caught the error.

sector.quote: Microsoft’s decision to replace human journalists with AI to run its news and search site MSN.com

failure_mode.quote: has been criticized after the automated system confused two mixed-race members of British pop group Little Mix

affected_population.quote: has been criticized after the automated system confused two mixed-race members of British pop group Little Mix
has been criticized after the automated system confused two mixed-race members of British pop group Little Mix

notes: Microsoft denied algorithmic bias; the exact cause was stated as an experimental image-selection feature.
